assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT turned the strongly correlated electron problem into a tractable, systematically improvable framework; combined with DFT it is now a working tool for Mott physics, heavy fermions, transition-metal oxides and magnetic materials. Original, conceptually clean (the infinite-dimension limit), and of lasting impact on how materials with localized orbitals are computed.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar are the natural trio; Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit, Georges-Kotliar's mapping onto an impurity model, and Kotliar's DFT+DMFT extension are distinct steps. Georges and Kotliar together with Vollhardt gives a defensible three-person configuration, but Metzner is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation by comparison with spectroscopy, cluster/extended variants and materials-specific work. Timely given long-standing recognition in the field, though it is a method rather than a single decisive observation.
uncertainties: Metzner's role in the original limit is not in the credited names, so the allocation is arguably incomplete.
Quantitative predictivity of DFT+DMFT depends on double counting and interaction parameters, which I cannot verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a new classification of band insulators by topology, with protected edge and surface states and large ensuing theory and materials programs. Original and conceptually deep.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp gives a clean three-person split between theory and experiment, though BHZ and three-dimensional TI work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents) complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Mature: HgTe edge transport, ARPES on Bi-based 3D TIs and many replications confirm the picture. Recognition is timely, with a Nobel-level 2016 topological prize already awarded for related ideas.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) lies outside the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize may be argued against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The flat-band prediction at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire quantum matter field, a highly tunable platform for correlated phases and magnetism in two dimensions.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 observations. The three supplied names form a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, with Cao and others as unrecognized contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature after about eight years, with independent replications, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and correlated states is still debated, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Role of earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and of the first-author experimentalists is not captured by the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping gave fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Clear, important invention.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance frontier; the two-person split is natural, although Hall and Hansch recognised frequency-comb enabling work earlier.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the laboratory with many independent clocks; timing is good as the SI second redefinition approaches.
uncertainties: Competing ion-clock contributions are outside this candidate.
Redefinition of the second is still pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions combined symmetry-filtered spin-dependent tunneling with practical devices, underpinning hard-disk read heads and MRAM. Strong link between first-principles theory and experiment, which I find persuasive.
assessment.attribution: Butler and Mathon independently predicted the effect from band-structure calculations; Yuasa and Parkin demonstrated it in 2004. Mathon is not in the supplied credit, and Parkin has already received recognition for GMR-related work, so the trio is an imperfect fit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely deployed; timeliness is plausible but the Nobel in 2007 for GMR may make it feel derivative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling and dispersive readout on a chip, becoming the architecture of superconducting quantum processors.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the architecture, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated it in 2004; the trio is clean. Overlap with other superconducting-qubit credit and the 2025 prize on macroscopic tunneling in circuits matters.
assessment.maturity: Mature and replicated worldwide; timely but close to the 2025 prize topic, which might cause hesitation.
uncertainties: Whether the achievement is physics-fundamental or enabling technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold-atom quantum simulation of Hubbard models, from the Mott transition to antiferromagnetic correlations, gives controlled access to correlated physics I care about from the theory side.
assessment.attribution: Greiner, Esslinger and Bloch realized the Mott-insulator and fermionic Hubbard regimes; Zoller and Jaksch's proposals are important but Zoller is omitted in this trio, creating an allocation puzzle.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, though fermionic simulations of the doped Hubbard model at the lowest temperatures remain an open frontier.
uncertainties: Several overlapping candidates (B008, B022) split the same field.
Whether simulations have yet answered a question that theory could not.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new window onto supermassive black-hole binaries and possible new physics.
assessment.attribution: Results come from several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA); selecting three people is hard and credit is clearly diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Premature: evidence is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma with no individual-source detection or firm Hellings-Downs confirmation at discovery level.
uncertainties: Astrophysical versus cosmological origin of the signal is not settled.
